{{Short description|Chern–Simons theory on infinite-dimensional manifolds}}
In [[mathematics]], '''infinite-dimensional Chern–Simons theory''' (not to be confused with [[∞-Chern–Simons theory]]) is a generalization of [[Chern–Simons theory]] to manifolds with infinite dimensions. These are not modeled with finite-dimensional [[Euclidean space|Euclidean spaces]], but infinite-dimensional [[Topological vector space|topological vector spaces]], for example [[Hilbert space|Hilbert]], [[Banach space|Banach]] and [[Fréchet space|Fréchet spaces]], which lead to [[Hilbert manifold|Hilbert]], [[Banach space|Banach]] and [[Fréchet manifold|Fréchet manifolds]] respectively. [[Principal bundle|Principal bundles]], which in finite-dimensional Chern–Simons theory are considered with ([[Compact space|compact]]) [[Lie group|Lie groups]] as gauge groups, are then fittingly considered with Hilbert Lie, Banach Lie and Fréchet Lie groups as gauge groups respectively, which also makes their total spaces into a Hilbert, Banach and Fréchet manifold respectively. These are called Hilbert, Banach and Fréchet principal bundles respectively. The theory is named after [[:de:Shiing-Shen_Chern|Shiing-Shen Chern]] and [[Jim Simons|James Simons]], who first described [[Chern–Simons form|Chern–Simons forms]] in 1974,<ref name=":18">{{cite journal |last1=Chern |first1=Shiing-Shen |author-link1=Shiing-Shen Chern |last2=Simons |first2=James |author-link2=Jim Simons |date=September 1996 |title=Characteristic forms and geometric invariants |journal=World Scientific Series in 20th Century Mathematics |language=en |volume=4 |pages=363–384 |doi=10.1142/9789812812834_0026|isbn=978-981-02-2385-4 }}</ref> although the generalization was not developed by them.
